lessons.title: Reversible reactions and equilibrium
lessons.programRef: GCE O Level Chemistry — Reversible reactions and equilibrium (basic), Haber and contact processes (to be checked against the official syllabus)
lessons.author: CastBridge (AI draft)
lessons.source: Original writing following the Cameroonian curriculum; to be reviewed by a teacher
objectives: Recognise a reversible reaction (⇌) and give examples.
Describe dynamic equilibrium in a closed system.
Predict the effect of changing temperature and pressure (Le Chatelier's principle).
Explain the conditions used in the Haber process.
reviewNotes: Haber process conditions quoted as 'about 450 °C, about 200 atmospheres, iron catalyst' are typical textbook figures; actual plants vary.
Le Chatelier's principle is stated qualitatively. Equilibrium constants are not part of this lesson.
Syllabus references, scope and level of difficulty are to be checked against the official text; all facts, formulas and worked examples to be verified by a teacher before release.

blocks.title: Reversible reactions
blocks.md: A **reversible reaction** can go both ways, shown by **⇌**. Examples: hydrated copper(II) sulphate (blue) ⇌ anhydrous copper(II) sulphate (white) + water; ammonium chloride ⇌ ammonia + hydrogen chloride; N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃. In a **closed system** the forward and reverse reactions eventually proceed at the **same rate**: this is **dynamic equilibrium** (the amounts stay constant but both reactions go on).

blocks.title: Le Chatelier's principle
blocks.md:
If a condition of a system at equilibrium is changed, the position of equilibrium shifts to **oppose** the change.

- **Higher pressure** favours the side with **fewer gas molecules**.
- **Higher temperature** favours the **endothermic** direction; lower temperature favours the exothermic direction.
- Removing a product pulls the equilibrium towards the products.
- A **catalyst** does not change the position of equilibrium; it only makes it reached faster.

blocks.title: The Haber process
blocks.md: N₂(g) + 3H₂(g) ⇌ 2NH₃(g); the forward reaction is **exothermic**. Four gas moles on the left, two on the right. Conditions: about **450 °C**, about **200 atmospheres**, **iron** catalyst. High pressure favours ammonia; low temperature would favour ammonia too but is too slow, so a **compromise** temperature is used. Unreacted N₂ and H₂ are recycled and ammonia is removed by cooling and liquefying.

blocks.title: Watch out
blocks.md:
- At equilibrium the reactions have **not stopped**; the rates are equal.
- A catalyst does not increase the yield at equilibrium.
- Do not say 'the reaction goes to completion' for a reversible reaction in a closed system.

blocks.caption: Rates of the forward and reverse reactions approach each other and become equal at equilibrium.
blocks.alt: A falling blue curve and a rising red curve meeting at the same value.

blocks.title: Example 1 — effect of pressure
blocks.statement: How does increasing the pressure affect the yield of ammonia in N₂ + 3H₂ ⇌ 2NH₃?
steps: Left side has 1 + 3 = 4 moles of gas, right side has 2 moles.
Higher pressure favours the side with fewer gas moles: the yield of ammonia **increases**.

blocks.title: Example 2 — effect of temperature
blocks.statement: The forward reaction in the Haber process is exothermic. Explain why a very high temperature would give a poor yield and why a moderate temperature of about 450 °C is chosen.
steps: Raising the temperature shifts the equilibrium in the endothermic direction, which is the reverse reaction, so less ammonia is present at equilibrium.
But at low temperature the rate is too slow, so about 450 °C with an iron catalyst is a compromise between yield and rate.
blocks.answer: High T lowers yield; 450 °C is a compromise

exercises.prompt: Ammonium chloride is warmed gently in a test tube: NH₄Cl(s) ⇌ NH₃(g) + HCl(g). Damp red litmus and damp blue litmus papers are placed in the mouth of the tube.

parts.prompt: Which paper changes first, and to what colour?
parts.explanation: NH₃ is lighter than HCl, diffuses faster and is alkaline.

parts.prompt: The white solid reforms on the cooler part of the tube. This shows that the reaction is
parts.explanation: NH₃ and HCl recombine on cooling to form NH₄Cl.
